notes: Site: IKEA UK (ikea.com/gb/en). Homepage mega-menu 'hot' links across many category sub-menus expose 'New products' pointing to https://www.ikea.com/gb/en/new/new-products/ (same base URL, only a subcategory filter query param differs per context - facet filters, not separate PLPs). Opened with Playwright (tier 2, after tier-1 HTTP fetch showed only client-rendered nav JSON). Page heading is 'New' / 'New products' with copy "Looking for the latest and greatest? Here is where you will find what's new. Explore our latest additions of affordable furniture and home decor." - a genuine 'recently added to catalogue' merchandising concept with a real browsable/sortable/filterable product grid (not a lookbook or campaign page). The page also shows department 'chips' (Outdoor, Storage furniture, Home organisation, Textiles & rugs, Sofas, Kitchens, Kitchenware & tableware, Baby & children, Decoration) - inspected their hrefs directly (e.g. https://www.ikea.com/gb/en/new/new-products/?filters=f-subcategories:od001&sort=NEWEST) and confirmed these are query-param filters of the SAME base /new/new-products/ listing, not distinct site-curated New Arrivals sub-pages, so no sub-categories were invented; only the canonical unfiltered URL is emitted. Header shows '1139 items' (shown twice) and the results-list footer independently confirms 'Showing 24 of 1139 results' - cross-checked, qty verified reliable. No 'New Collection'-style editorial page found needing the ambiguous-collection review; no other New Arrivals-labelled entry point found in nav, footer, or search.
